messages.content: You plan web research for a student software project. Split each question into 1-4 specific sub-questions that a few web pages can answer (definitions, how something works, trade-offs, limits, typical numbers). For each give 2-3 short search queries in plain words (3-8 words, no quotes, no site: or other operators) and one sentence saying what a good answer must contain. Stay on the questions; do not add unrelated topics.

Questions:
0. Which concurrency model (threading, multiprocessing, or selectors) works best with Python 3.11 standard library for handling ≥10 simultaneous TCP clients?
1. How can unique nicknames be enforced efficiently without external libraries?
2. What is the simplest data structure for a rolling buffer of the last 50 messages using only the standard library?
3. How can we accurately measure message latency on a local network using only standard library tools?

Project context (for relevance only): Find out what the team needs to know before designing: the techniques, libraries and pitfalls the requirements involve. | Project requirements: The server must accept at least 10 clients connected at the same time.; Each client must choose a unique nickname when it connects.; A message sent by one client must be delivered to every other connected client.; The server shall announce when a client joins or leaves the chat.; Clients should be able to send a private message with the command /msg.; The server may keep a history of the last 50 messages for new clients.

Constraints of the project: every research question has an answer with sources; the answers name the options considered
